questions.question: In which year did Rudolf Virchow develop his ideas by publishing his famous formula 'Omnis cellula-e cellula', which became a part of the foundation of cell theory?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1855**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Rudolf Virchow** was a renowned **German **physician, anthropologist, pathologist, prehistorian, biologist, and politician.
 
• In **1855**, Virchow published his famous formula** *'Omnis cellula-e cellula'***, which translates to **"every cell originates from another existing cell like it"**.
 
• This concept became a fundamental part of the **cell theory**, which is a cornerstone of modern biology.
 
• The cell theory explains that all living organisms are composed of cells, and the cell is the basic unit of life.
 
• Virchow’s work was crucial in understanding the process of cell division and the continuity of life.

questions.question: Meera shifted to a new house and was fixing light bulbs in her apartment. One of the three bulbs she fixed did not light up. Upon testing she realised it was a case of fused bulb. So, she bought a new one which then lit up perfectly. Select the correct option that describes what happened to the fused bulb.

options.text: The switch for the bulb was not turned on
Meera did not fix the bulb to the holder properly
The filament inside it was broken
There was no connection between the bulb holder and the switch

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The filament inside it was broken**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• When a **light bulb** does not light up, it is often due to a **broken filament**.
 
• The **filament** is a thin wire inside the bulb that **glows** when an electric current passes through it.
 
• If the filament is broken, the **circuit is incomplete**, and electricity cannot flow through it to produce light.
 
• This is a common issue with **incandescent bulbs**, where the filament is made of **tungsten**.
 
• Over time, the filament can **wear out** or break due to **thermal stress** and repeated heating and cooling cycles.
 
• Replacing the bulb with a new one that has an intact filament resolves the issue, as seen in Meera's case.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **The switch for the bulb was not turned on**

 
 
• Sometimes, a bulb may not light up simply because the **switch** controlling it is **off**.
 
• This is a basic troubleshooting step to ensure the switch is in the **on position** before checking for other issues.
 
 
 
• **Meera did not fix the bulb to the holder properly**
 
 
• If a bulb is not **properly screwed** into the holder, it may not make the necessary **electrical contact** to light up.
 
• Ensuring the bulb is **securely fixed** can sometimes solve the problem.
 
 
 
• **There was no connection between the bulb holder and the switch**
 
 
• A **loose wire** or **faulty connection** between the bulb holder and the switch can prevent the bulb from lighting up.
 
• This issue requires checking the **wiring** and ensuring all connections are **secure**.

questions.question: The primary function of which globular structure is to produce and assemble the ribosomes of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleolus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **nucleolus** is a prominent sub-structure within the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
 
• Its primary function is to **produce and assemble ribosome components**.
 
• It is composed of proteins, DNA, and RNA, and it is the site where **ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is synthesized**.
 
• After synthesis, the rRNA combines with proteins to form **ribosomal subunits**, which are then exported to the cytoplasm.
 
• The nucleolus plays a critical role in the cell's ability to produce proteins, as ribosomes are the cellular machinery responsible for protein synthesis.
 
• It is also involved in **cell cycle regulation** and the response to cellular stress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chromatin**__

 __
 
• **Chromatin** is a complex of DNA and protein found in eukaryotic cells.
 
• Its primary functions are to package DNA into a more compact, denser shape, and to regulate gene expression and DNA replication.
 
• Chromatin is found in the nucleus and can be seen as either euchromatin (less condensed) or heterochromatin (more condensed).
 
 
 
• **Centriole**__
 __
 
• A **centriole** is a cylindrical cell structure composed mainly of a protein called tubulin.
 
• Centriole functions primarily in cell division, where it helps in the formation of the spindle fibers that separate chromosomes.
 
• They are also involved in the formation of cilia and flagella, which are important for cell movement.
 
 
 
• **Peroxisomes**__
 
 
• **Peroxisomes** are small, membrane-bound organelles found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells.
 
• They contain enzymes that oxidize certain molecules normally found in the cell, notably fatty acids and amino acids.
 
• Peroxisomes play a key role in metabolism, detoxification, and reactive oxygen species detoxification.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is true?

A. Igneous rocks are used as fuel by igniting them.

B. Sedimentary rocks can never change into metamorphic rocks or magma.

C. Igneous rocks can change into sedimentary rocks over a long period of time.

D. Magma can form sedimentary rocks on cooling.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Igneous rocks can change into sedimentary rocks over a long period of time.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Igneous rocks** are formed from the solidification of **magma or lava**.
 
• Over a long period, **weathering and erosion** can break down igneous rocks into smaller particles.
 
• These particles can be transported by natural agents like **wind, water, and ice** and deposited in layers.
 
• Over time, the accumulated layers are compacted and cemented to form **sedimentary rocks**.
 
• This process is part of the **rock cycle**, which describes the transformation of rock types over geological time scales.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Igneous rocks**__

 __
 
• These rocks are not used as fuel because they do not contain combustible materials.
 
• Examples include **granite, basalt, and pumice**.
 
 
 
• **Sedimentary rocks**__
 __
 
• These rocks can transform into **metamorphic rocks** under high pressure and temperature.
 
• They can also melt into **magma** if subjected to extreme conditions.
 
• Examples include **limestone, sandstone, and shale**.
 
 
 
• **Magma**__
 
 
• When magma cools and solidifies, it forms **igneous rocks**, not sedimentary rocks.
 
• Magma is a molten rock found beneath the Earth's surface.

questions.question: What is the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**9.8 m/s²**__.

• The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth is **9.8 m/s²**.
 
• This value represents the acceleration that objects experience when falling freely towards the Earth.
 
• The value of 9.8 m/s² is derived from the **gravitational constant (G)** and the **mass and radius of the Earth**.
 
• **Gravity **is a force that attracts two bodies towards each other, and it is crucial for maintaining the orbits of planets and satellites.
 
• The standard value of 9.8 m/s² is used in various calculations in physics and engineering, such as projectile motion and free-fall equations.
 
• The unit of acceleration due to gravity is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India grants citizens the right to freedom of speech and expression, freedom of assembly and freedom to practice any profession?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 19**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 19** of the **Constitution of India** provides for the protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
 
• It guarantees the citizens of India the **right to freedom of speech and expression**.
 
• It also includes the **freedom to assemble peacefully without arms**.
 
• Additionally, it encompasses the **freedom to practice any profession** or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business.
 
• These freedoms are subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the state in the interests of **sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the state, friendly relations with foreign states, public order, decency, or morality**, or in relation to contempt of court, defamation, or incitement to an offense.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 17**__

 __
 
• Article 17 of the **Indian Constitution** abolishes **untouchability**.
 
• It forbids its practice in any form.
 
• The enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability shall be an offense punishable in accordance with the law.
 
 
 
• **Article 18**__
 __
 
• **Article 18** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the **abolition of titles**.
 
• It prohibits the state from conferring any titles, except military and academic distinctions.
 
• It also forbids Indian citizens from accepting any titles from a foreign state.
 
 
 
• **Article 25**__
 
 
• Article 25 of the **Indian Constitution** guarantees **freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion**.
 
• This freedom is subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• It also provides for the state to regulate or restrict any economic, financial, political, or other secular activity associated with religious practice.

questions.question: What is u in the equation s = ut + 1/2 at², which represents the position-time relation?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Initial velocity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the equation **s = ut + 1/2 at²**, **u** stands for the **initial velocity** of the object.
 
• This equation is one of the fundamental equations of motion in classical mechanics, often referred to as the **second equation of motion**.
 
• The term **s** represents the **displacement** or position change of the object.
 
• The term **t** represents the **time** duration over which the motion occurs.
 
• The term **a** stands for the **acceleration** of the object.
 
• The equation combines **initial velocity (u)**, **acceleration (a)**, and **time (t)** to determine the **displacement (s)**.
 
• This equation is derived from the basic principles of **Newtonian mechanics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform acceleration**__

 __
 
• **Uniform acceleration** refers to a constant rate of change in velocity.
 
• In equations of motion, **acceleration (a)** is often assumed to be uniform.
 
 
 
• **Speed of the object**__
 __
 
• **Speed** is a scalar quantity representing how fast an object is moving.
 
• Speed does not include direction, unlike velocity, which is a vector quantity.
 
 
 
• **Change in momentum**__
 
 
• **Momentum** is the product of the mass and velocity of an object.
 
• The change in momentum is often described by the impulse-momentum theorem.

questions.question:
In the ecosystem, there can be multiple food chains, but only a limited number of trophic levels. Based on this statement which of the following is NOT true?

A: Each level in the food chain represents one trophic level

B: Organisms in the lowest trophic level have the highest population as a lot of energy is available for their survival

C: There is a loss of energy as it is being absorbed by organisms at the higher trophic level

D: Organisms at the highest trophic level make their own food and do not fully depend on the lower trophic organisms for energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Trophic levels in an ecosystem represent different stages of **energy transfer**, starting from producers to top consumers.
 
• **Energy transfer** between trophic levels is not 100% efficient; a significant portion of energy is lost as heat, respiration, etc.
 
• **Producers** (like plants) occupy the lowest trophic level and have the highest biomass and energy availability.
 
• **Consumers** (herbivores, carnivores) occupy higher trophic levels and depend on lower trophic levels for energy.
 
• Organisms at the highest trophic level, such as top predators, rely heavily on the energy provided by organisms at lower trophic levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Producers**: Occupy the first trophic level and include **photosynthetic organisms** like plants and algae.
 
• **Primary Consumers**: Herbivores that feed on producers, such as **deer and rabbits**.
 
• **Secondary Consumers**: Carnivores that feed on primary consumers, like **wolves and snakes**.
 
• **Tertiary Consumers**: Top predators that feed on secondary consumers, such as **eagles and sharks**.

questions.question:

A. On solidification, molten magma forms sedimentary rocks.

B. Igneous rocks can be intrusive or extrusive.

C. Under the effect of high temperatures and pressure, sedimentary rocks change to metamorphic rocks.

D. Under the effect of high temperatures and pressure, igneous rocks change to metamorphic rocks.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**FTTT**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Sedimentary rocks** are formed from **sediments** compacted and cemented over time, not from the solidification of **molten magma**.
 
• **Igneous rocks** can indeed be classified as **intrusive** (formed inside the Earth) or **extrusive** (formed on the Earth's surface).
 
• Under high **temperatures** and **pressure**, **sedimentary rocks** can transform into **metamorphic rocks**.
 
• Similarly, under high **temperature** and **pressure**, **igneous rocks** can also change to **metamorphic rocks**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Sedimentary Rocks**

 
 
• These rocks are often formed in **layers** and can contain **fossils**.
 
• Examples include **limestone**, **sandstone**, and **shale**.
 
• They are typically formed from **particles** deposited by **water**, **wind**, or **ice**.
 
 
 
• **Intrusive Igneous Rocks**
 
 
• These rocks form **slowly** beneath the Earth's surface, allowing **large crystals** to develop.
 
• Common examples include **granite** and **diorite**.
 
 
 
• **Extrusive Igneous Rocks**
 
 
• These rocks form **quickly** on the Earth's surface, resulting in **small crystals** or a **glassy texture**.
 
• Examples include **basalt** and **pumice**.
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Rocks**
 
 
• These rocks are formed from **pre-existing rocks** (igneous, sedimentary, or other metamorphic rocks) through **metamorphism**.
 
• Examples include **marble** (from limestone) and **schist** (from shale).

questions.question:
Choose the correct statement/s from the following.

i. It is difficult to carry one's wealth under a barter system of transactions.

ii. Money is perishable and it cannot be stored.

iii. An increase in the price level can diminish the purchasing power of currency.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**i and iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under a **barter system**, it is indeed **difficult to carry one's wealth** because wealth is in the form of goods and services, which are **bulky and perishable**. This makes transactions cumbersome and inefficient. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Unlike many goods in a barter system, money is not perishable and can be stored over time without losing its value (except in cases of inflation). *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• An **increase in the price level (inflation) can diminish the purchasing power of currency**. This means that with higher prices, the same amount of money can buy fewer goods and services. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Barter System**__

 __
 
• The barter system is an ancient method of exchange where goods and services are traded directly without using money.
 
• One major drawback is the "double coincidence of wants" problem, where both parties need to have what the other wants.
 
 
 
• **Inflation**__
 __
 
• Inflation is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises, eroding purchasing power.
 
• Central banks attempt to limit inflation, and avoid deflation, to keep the economy running smoothly.
 
 
 
• **Currency**__
 
 
• Currency serves as a medium of exchange, a unit of account, a store of value, and sometimes, a standard of deferred payment.
 
• Unlike goods in a barter system, modern currency is durable and can be stored over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Scurvy** is a disease resulting from a deficiency of **Vitamin C**.
 
• It is characterized by symptoms such as **fatigue, swollen gums, joint pain, and anemia**.
 
• Vitamin C is essential for the **synthesis of collagen**, which is important for the maintenance of skin, blood vessels, and bones.
 
• The disease was historically common among sailors who did not have access to fresh fruits and vegetables during long voyages.
 
• Scurvy can be prevented by consuming sufficient amounts of **Vitamin C-rich foods** such as citrus fruits, tomatoes, and leafy greens.
 
• Early detection and treatment with Vitamin C supplements can reverse the symptoms of scurvy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Goitre**__

 __
 
• **Goitre** is an abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland.
 
• It is commonly caused by an **iodine deficiency** in the diet.
 
• Symptoms can include a visible swelling in the neck and difficulty swallowing.
 
 
 
• **Atherosclerosis**__
 __
 
• **Atherosclerosis** is a condition where the arteries become narrowed and hardened due to a buildup of plaque.
 
• This can lead to serious problems such as **heart attacks and strokes**.
 
• It is typically related to factors such as a high-fat diet, smoking, and lack of exercise.
 
 
 
• **Pellagra**__
 
 
• **Pellagra** is a disease caused by a deficiency of **niacin (Vitamin B3)**.
 
• It is characterized by symptoms including **dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia**.
 
• Pellagra was historically prevalent in populations that relied heavily on maize as a staple food.

questions.question: The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill 2023 aims to make the _____________ only conclusive age proof that can be used as a single document for various purposes.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Birth Certificate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill 2023** aims to streamline the process of using a **Birth Certificate** as the only conclusive age proof.
 
• A **Birth Certificate** will serve as a single document for various purposes such as **admission to educational institutions, issuing of driving licenses, passports, and Aadhaar cards**.
 
• This amendment will help in reducing the need for multiple documents and simplify administrative procedures.
 
• The bill aims to create a more **efficient and reliable system** for managing and verifying age-related information.
 
• A **centralized database** will be created to maintain the records, ensuring better coordination and accessibility.
 
• This measure will also aid in the prevention of **identity fraud** and ensure that individuals have a single, official document that can be universally accepted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ST/SC/OBC Certificate**__

 __
 
• These certificates are issued to individuals belonging to specific **Scheduled Tribes (ST), Scheduled Castes (SC), and Other Backward Classes (OBC)** to avail reservations and benefits under government schemes.
 
• They are not used as age proof but rather for verifying eligibility for various social and educational benefits.
 
 
 
• **Aadhar Card**__
 __
 
• The **Aadhar Card** is a unique identification number issued to residents of India by the **Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI)**.
 
• While it contains demographic and biometric data, it is not specifically designed as a conclusive age proof.
 
 
 
• **Voter ID**__
 
 
• The **Voter ID** is issued by the **Election Commission of India** to adult citizens of India for the purpose of voting.
 
• It serves as an identity proof but is not primarily used for age verification.
